Different members may be eligible for different offers, so you’ll want to log into your account to see what you’re eligible for. However, it appears that the best version of the offer is for up to a 100% bonus, structured as follows:

I should emphasize that other members seem to be eligible for offers of 85%, 90%, or 95%, so it’s no guarantee that everyone will see the 100% offer.

Ordinarily, Air Canada Aeroplan charges $0.0375 CAD (~0.026 USD) per point. Any purchases made with US credit cards and US billing addresses aren’t subject to sales tax either.

If you purchased 500,000 Aeroplan points with a 100% bonus, you’d receive a total of 1,000,000 Aeroplan points at a cost of $18,750 CAD (~$13,101 USD), which is a rate of 1.31 cents (USD) per Aeroplan point.

If you wanted to purchase the fewest possible points at the best possible price, you’d want to buy exactly 90,000 points at a cost of $3,375 CAD (~$2,358 USD), which would potentially get you 180,000 points, for the same cost per point.

While you can purchase up to one million Aeroplan points per account per calendar year, there’s ordinarily a per-transaction limit of 250,000 points pre-bonus. However, during this promotion that has been doubled, to 500,000 points.

Aeroplan points purchases typically post pretty close to instantly, though in some situations, it could take up to 72 hours for points to post. Note that the purchase of Aeroplan points is non-refundable, and Aeroplan points purchases also don’t count toward elite status.

When Air Canada Aeroplan offer a promotion on purchased points, we most commonly see a bonus in the range of 90-110%, but the exact offers do vary. Personally I’d buy points based on when you’re ready to redeem them, rather than the exact cost. After all, the cost to buy points with a 100% bonus vs. a 110% bonus isn’t vastly different.

Below is a chart with some of the recent promotions we saw from the Aeroplan program, before this one.

Air Canada Aeroplan points purchases are processed by points.com, meaning they don’t count as an airfare purchase for the purposes of credit card spending. Therefore I’d recommend using a card on which you’re trying to reach a minimum spending requirement, or otherwise, a credit card that maximizes your return on everyday spending.

Since the purchase of Aeroplan points is billed in CAD, there is one other great option. The Atmos™ Rewards Summit Visa Infinite® Credit Card (learn more) offers 3x points on foreign purchases, so that’s a fantastic card for this kind of purchase. Beyond that, the best options would be cards that offer 2x transferable points, while having no foreign transaction fees.

Aeroplan is one of my favorite frequent flyer programs out there. To cover a few of the basics:

There are lots of phenomenal uses of Aeroplan points, and this is a program that I redeem through regularly. Just keep in mind that Aeroplan now has dynamic award pricing on select partners, including Emirates, Etihad, FlyDubai, and United, among others.

One of my favorite things about Air Canada Aeroplan is that the program has more airline partners than any other frequent flyer program, and you can redeem points on over 45 airlines. In addition to Air Canada belonging to the Star Alliance, Aeroplan also partners with airlines that include Etihad, Azul, Air Serbia, Virgin Australia, Air Dolomiti, Eurowings, Gulf Air, Oman Air, Air Mauritius, and Emirates.

Always look up award availability before buying points, to get a sense of what you can expect.

Many consumers are frustrated by the practice of airlines adding carrier imposed surcharges to award tickets. In the case of Aeroplan, there are no fuel surcharges on award tickets, meaning you shouldn’t expect to pay big fees when redeeming points.

Everyone will value points currencies differently. Based on my latest miles & points valuations, I consider Aeroplan points to be worth 1.4 cents each. However, I tend to value points pretty conservatively, and there are many ways to get way more value from Aeroplan points than that.

Air Canada Aeroplan points only expire after 18 months of inactivity. However, any account activity that leads to earning or redeeming points (including buying them) would reset the expiration.

While buying Aeroplan points could represent a great deal, keep in mind that there are lots of other ways to earn Aeroplan points. Most significantly, Aeroplan is transfer partners with American Express Membership Rewards, Bilt Rewards, Capital One, and Chase Ultimate Rewards, making the currency pretty easy to acquire. From all those currencies, rewards transfer at a 1:1 ratio, and sometimes you’ll even find transfer bonuses.

On top of that, in the United States there’s the Chase Air Canada Aeroplan® Credit Card (learn more), which is pretty lucrative.

Air Canada’s Aeroplan program is offering a bonus on purchased points. While people may be targeted for different offers, it appears the best offer is for up to a 100% bonus, which kicks in as long as you purchase at least 90,000 points in one transaction. This is an opportunity to buy points for 1.31 cents (in USD) each.

This could represent a good deal, and there are plenty of situations under which the math will work out for this promotion. Still, in general I’d only recommend buying points with a short term use in mind, as there’s always risk to holding onto points for longer periods of time.

Do you plan on buying Aeroplan points with this promotion?

#6219. Alaska Atmos Rewards Business Card Bonus: 90K Points Welcome Offer

The $195 annual fee Atmos™ Rewards Visa Signature® Business Card currently has a huge bonus of 90,000 Atmos Rewards points after spending $6,000 within the first 90 days. For context, this is the business card of the Atmos Rewards portfolio, the loyalty program of Alaska and Hawaiian. This is a potentially lucrative card that has just undergone a refresh, and you can read my Atmos Rewards Business Card review here.

In this post I’d like to go over the details of the Atmos Rewards Business Card bonus, for anyone who may be considering applying. There are lots of reasons to get this card, particularly the incredible bonus.

Link: Learn more about the Atmos™ Rewards Visa Signature® Business Card with 90K bonus points

The Atmos Rewards Business Card currently has a welcome offer of 90,000 Atmos Rewards bonus points after spending $6,000 within the first 90 days.

Based on my latest miles & points valuations, I consider Atmos Rewards points to be worth 1.5 cents each, meaning the 90,000 points are worth $1,350 to me, which is among the best bonuses out there. There are lots of great uses of Atmos Rewards points, for travel on Alaska, Hawaiian, oneworld partners, and non-alliance partners.

Atmos Rewards points have all kinds of uses, ranging from booking short haul one-way economy awards on American for 4,500 points, to booking Starlux business class one-way awards from the US to Asia for 75,000 points. Of course capacity controls apply, so patience and flexibility will be required to get the best deal. Still, I find this to be one of the most useful points currencies out there.

The Atmos Rewards Business Card 90,000-point offer is the best publicly available sign-up bonus that we’ve seen on the card since it launched in August 2025 (which is when the Atmos Rewards program formally launched). How do the previous Atmos Rewards Business Card bonuses compare?

As you can see, the Atmos Rewards Business Card sign-up bonus has varied from 70,000 points to 90,000 points, and the current bonus of 90,000 points is the best publicly available offer we’ve seen. So if there has ever been a time to apply for this card, this is it.

When it comes to getting approved for the Atmos Rewards Business Card, what rules should you be aware of? There are the card specific policies, and then also the more generic Bank of America policies. When you pull up the application, you’ll see the following terms:

This one-time promotion is limited to company level Business Card clients opening a new account in response to this offer and will not apply to requests to convert existing accounts.

The good news is that eligibility for the Atmos Rewards Business Card is considered completely independently of any other cards in the portfolio, so you’re eligible if you have either of the personal Atmos Rewards credit cards. Many people even report being eligible for the Atmos Rewards Business Card (including the bonus) if they’ve had it in the past.

Beyond that, Bank of America doesn’t have many consistent restrictions when it comes to getting approved for business cards. While Bank of America has the 2/3/4 rule and 3/12 rules, those apply to personal cards, and not business cards. Generally those with a Bank of America banking relationship also have the best odds of approval (though it’s by no means a requirement).

There’s not a consistent credit score you need to have to be approved for this card, though personally I’d hope to have a score in the “good” to “excellent” range, ideally 700+ points. However, people with lower scores have been approved, and people with higher scores have been rejected.

Applying for this card won’t count as a further card toward Chase’s 5/24 rule, in case that’s a limit you’re trying to stay under.

Beyond the great bonus, there are multiple reasons to consider the $195 annual fee Atmos Rewards Business Card:

If you fly Alaska or Hawaiian with any frequency, then having this card should be a no-brainer. The benefits really add up, between the lounge passes, the first checked bag free, preferred boarding, savings on inflight purchases, and more.

The Atmos Rewards Business Card has introduced a best-ever welcome offer, whereby you can earn 90,000 Atmos Rewards points upon completing minimum spending.

This is an exceptional bonus, and this card is absolutely worth picking up for the points, especially given that eligibility isn’t mutually exclusive with other Atmos Rewards cards. In the long run, the card can be worth it for the perks for travel on Alaska and Hawaiian.

Anecdotally I find Bank of America business cards to be quite easy to get approved for, including if you’ve had the card in the past. Applying for this card also shouldn’t count as a further card toward the Chase 5/24 limit, if that’s of concern to you.

Anyone plan to pick up the Atmos Rewards Business Card with this great offer?

#6216. Finnair Celebrates International Men’s Day With All-Male Crew On Flight

There’s still quite a gender gap in the airline industry, with a disproportionate number of pilots being male, and a disproportionate number of flight attendants being female. Airlines will sometimes have special celebrations with all-female crews, so here’s an interesting twist on that.

Today is (apparently) International Men’s Day. We often see airlines commemorate International Women’s Day, but there aren’t many airlines that celebrate the equivalent for men… well, except Finnair! The airline has today operated its annual flight with an all-male crew. This was the case for Finnair flight AY1331, from Helsinki (HEL) to London (LHR), using an Airbus A350-900.

The crew consisted of 10 people, comprised of two pilots and eight flight attendants. The gate agents were also all men. So, why is this important? Finnair highlights how only around 10% of cabin crew at the airline are male, but the company hopes to see that number grow in the future.

I think this is a fun concept, and it would be nice to see a closer to 50/50 gender ratio in both the cockpit and cabin, as it would show that everyone is given a fair chance at such a career.

I think it’s worth acknowledging that at many airlines, hiring of flight attendants is still primarily or exclusively based on gender. Now, the policies do vary significantly by airline, but perhaps an extreme example is India’s largest airline, IndiGo, which only hires female flight attendants. It’s literally written on the application, that it’s a job for “Female Indian nationals.”

It’s all so strange, because the airline has this super enthusiastic page about the importance of diversity in the workplace, and says “all employment decisions are made solely on the basis of merit and qualifications, without regard to a candidate’s gender…” You mean except the single largest portion of your workforce, which is cabin crew?

What’s interesting is that while those gender restrictions exist in the cabin, roughly 18% of the carrier’s pilots are female, which is way above the global average of 7%. That’s obviously a conscious effort, so I guess the idea is that women can become pilots but men can’t become flight attendants.

In fairness, I suspect part of the motivation here is that IndiGo flight attendants share hotel rooms on layovers, and that is a bit more complicated with mixed genders. Then again, it seems easy enough to just try to pair male flight attendants on trips, so it’s hardly a hurdle that can’t be overcome.

While we’re used to seeing airlines celebrate International Women’s Day, it’s rare to see an airline celebrating International Men’s Day. Finnair has operated an all-male flight today, intended to highlight how only 10% of flight attendants at the airline are male, and the airline wants to change that. While an unconventional initiative nowadays, I think this is still pretty cool.

What do you make of Finnair’s all-male flight?

#6215. Amex Auto-Enrolling Card Members In Paperless Billing (Sorry, Dad!)

Dad, here’s a blog post you should pay attention to (and thanks to Steve for flagging this)…

With banks, it’s typically possible to get your account statements by email or mail. There’s no denying that consumer preferences have shifted over the years, and along those lines, Amex has just sent an email to card members, informing them that “we’re making the switch to paperless.” Here’s the main part of the email:

We’re making the switch to paperless billing statements and account communications, beginning February 2027.

Here’s what happens nextWe want to help you get ready to make the switch too. So, we’ve enrolled your account listed above in the paperless delivery option – but for now, we’ll continue to send you communications about your account in the mail. We’ll also mail your billing statements for the closing dates of November 2026, December 2026, and January 2027.

After that, we’ll send account communications to you by email, and you’ll receive your monthly billing statements electronically. When they’re ready, you’ll be able to view them anytime by logging in to your account online at americanexpress.com or in the American Express App.

Now, that makes it sound like people will be forced to switch to paperless billing, but I don’t believe that’s actually the case? Because further down in the email, it says this:

Not ready to go paperless? No problem! You can re-enroll in paper billing statements and account communications by going to americanexpress.com/paperlesssettings, selecting “U.S. Mail,” and following the prompts to opt back in.

So it seems like what’s happening here is that Amex will try to force everyone into paperless billing by making it the default, but maybe those who specifically once again state their preferences for paper billing will be able to maintain that communication method?

Suffice it to say that going back 25 years, a vast majority of people got paper statements for their credit cards, while nowadays a vast majority of people get paperless statements, obviously reflecting the shift we’ve seen in how the internet is used.

It’s funny, because I’m sure 99% of OMAAT readers would be confused at the thought of getting paper bills, and would wonder what purpose that serves. But then there are also people like my dad, who rely on paper statements for their credit cards, pay their statement by phone, etc.

So it does sound like people will have the option of opting back into paper billing after being auto-enrolled in paperless billing, so the concept isn’t being eliminated altogether. Still, for my dad, there would likely be quite the learning curve.

Then again, up until less than a decade ago he didn’t have a cell phone and insisted he didn’t need one, while now he kind of loves it, for everything from texting, to Googling all kinds of stuff. That’s of course a double-edged sword as well, because he seems to believe that if the Google AI summary says something, it must be true. We’re not talking things like vaccines. Instead, we’re talking things like whether the salmon at Red Lobster is good, etc. Anyway, I digress…

As of February 2027, Amex will be automatically moving those with paper billing to paperless billing. While the message makes it sound like people will be forced to switch to paperless billing, that doesn’t seem to be the case, as Amex is also telling people they can once again enroll in paper billing statements and account communications if they’re “not ready to go paperless.” So Amex just seems to be trying to thin the ranks here of those using this feature.

What do you make of Amex’s switch to paperless billing?

Taking a cruise is even better when you get a great deal — and if you’re looking to book right now for a cruise (or cruises) in 2027 and beyond, your timing couldn’t be better. Cruise lines have launched Black Friday deals that include discounted fares, cabin upgrades, third- and fourth-guest-free promos, and onboard credits.

We’ve found the best promotions from leading ocean and river cruise lines, lesser-known small-ship operators and expedition brands. So whether your goal is beach time in the Caribbean, wildlife-spotting in Alaska, seeing the northern lights in the Arctic or enjoying culture and cuisine along Europe’s rivers, there’s a deal for every type of cruiser.

When considering Black Friday offers, however, remember that cruise demand remains high, so selection may be limited and fares — especially on the newest ships — will likely be pricier than in years past. To truly get a good deal, make sure you’re comfortable with the final price quoted, including the exact fare per person and the value of any added perks, before booking. Calling the cruise line’s reservations department may help clarify any questions.

Here’s a look at the Black Friday deals being offered by more than 40 cruise lines. Check back soon for Cyber Monday deal updates.

Through Dec. 3, AmaWaterways has a Black Friday offer that lets you choose between a complimentary pre- or postcruise land package or cruise fare savings of up to $2,500 per cabin (double occupancy). You’ll also receive a free cabin upgrade on select 2027 and 2028 sailings in Europe and South America.

Small-ship operator American Cruise Lines’ current cruise deals and special offers include free domestic airfare and savings of $1,000 to $2,000 per cabin on select late 2026 and 2027 departures. This applies to its eight-night Florida Gulf Coast and Keys sailings, eight-night Southeast Sea Islands cruises, eight-night Columbia and Snake River sailings, and eight-night Lower Mississippi River cruises.

From Nov. 24 to 28, you can enjoy Black Friday savings of up to 55% on select expedition cruises from Atlas Ocean Voyages and also receive air credit savings of up to $2,000 per suite on qualifying voyages. Through Nov. 23, guests and travel advisers may also submit priority reservations for eligible expeditions on the Atlas Ocean Voyages website ahead of the five-day Black Friday promotional event. Reservations will begin confirming Nov. 24, subject to availability, with Atlas Yacht Club members receiving first priority to secure special Black Friday savings once the sale begins.

Through Dec. 12, Avalon Waterways is offering a Black Friday Sales Event featuring free gratuities and free airfare on select 2027 European river cruises. Avalon’s offer also includes savings of up to $2,000 per couple on a Panorama or Royal Suite upgrade on certain 2027 departures.

The Black Friday Flash Sale at Azamara, available now through Dec. 4, includes up to $6,000 off per cabin on select sailings in the Mediterranean, South America, Japan and Alaska, plus up to $750 in onboard credit per cabin. The deal is valid on all four Azamara ships for sailings from January 2027 to April 2028. You can book a sale voyage online or via a travel adviser.

Carnival's Black Friday deals span Black Friday, Cyber Monday and Travel Tuesday with promotions that include discounted fares (four-night sailings start at under $200 per person), $49 per person deposits, room upgrades starting at $1, "Kids Sail Free" offers on select cruises (in third and fourth bunks), discounted beverage and Wi-Fi and shore excursion packages, and up to $50 in onboard credits. Sales and promotions are rolling out through Dec. 1.

Celebrity Cruises has a rolling Black Friday promotion offering savings of 75% on the second guest in the cabin on hundreds of applicable sailings in 2027 and 2028, including Caribbean and Mediterranean voyages on its newest ship, Celebrity Xcel. There are also limited-time offers that include up to $1,000 in additional savings per cabin plus $100 savings on select European sailings. This offer, for example, is valid through Nov. 24.

Through Dec. 2, Greek cruise line Celestyal has a “Big Sailaway” Black Friday promotion offering savings of up to 50%, plus third and fourth guests in a cabin sail free, on 58 Mediterranean and Greek islands voyages (from three nights to 14 nights) departing between March 2027 and February 2028. Celestyal operates two mid-size ships, Celestyal Journey and Celestyal Discovery.

Italy-based Costa Cruises is celebrating the start of the holiday season with a Black Friday sale offering fares as low as $399 per person (double occupancy) on select departures through June 2027, when reserved by Nov. 30. The included regions are the Caribbean (on Costa Fascinosa and Costa Favolosa), the Canary Islands (on Costa Smeralda) and the Mediterranean (on Costa Pacifica, Costa Toscana, Costa Smeralda, Costa Fascinosa and Costa Favolosa).

Through Dec. 7, small luxury cruise line Cruise Croatia is offering Black Friday savings of up to $500 per cabin on select seven-night spring and summer 2027 Adriatic sailings between Dubrovnik and Split, Croatia.

Book by Dec. 2 to take advantage of the Seasonal Savings deal offered by luxury cruise line Crystal. It can save you up to 40% on more than 200 upcoming voyages worldwide on Crystal Serenity or Crystal Symphony. The discount applies only to the first and second guest in a cabin. Full World Cruise and Full Grand Journeys are excluded.

Through Dec. 7, the Cunard Black Friday event can save you up to 40% on select sailings aboard Cunard's four ships — Queen Elizabeth, Queen Victoria, Queen Mary 2 and Queen Anne — with fares starting at $999 per person. Plus, you’ll enjoy a 10% refundable deposit and an onboard credit. Deals are available on Caribbean, Northern Europe, Mediterranean, transatlantic and Canada sailings. Guests booking Grill Suites will also have their Hotel Charge waived.

Although Disney Cruise Line doesn’t have Black Friday-specific deals, it is currently offering savings of up to 25% on select Caribbean sailings from Fort Lauderdale, Port Canaveral and Galveston, Texas; it's also offering deals on Mexican Riviera sailings from San Diego. These three- to seven-night cruises must be booked under the "guaranteed stateroom with restrictions" category. (In this case, "guaranteed" means you can’t select your specific room, but you're guaranteed one in the category you’ve booked or higher.) Your specific cabin will be assigned at a later date, but a full, nonrefundable payment is due at the time of booking.

Through Dec. 1, save up to 40% with Black Friday offers when you book select sailings with luxury cruise line Explora Journeys. Choose from two options: Full Payment Fare with savings of up to 40% (full payment is required at the time of reservation and is nonrefundable and cannot be changed), or Flexible Fare with savings of up to 30% (a 5% deposit is required, and standard cancellation policies apply).

Grand Circle Cruise Line is offering Black Friday sales to travelers 50 and older with savings of up to $3,000 per person on select January to July 2027 river cruises in Europe. Or you can get a $500 per-person discount plus an additional 10% off all 2027 departures when you pay in full. You can reserve by Nov. 30 by calling 800-221-2610 with code "BLACKFRIDAY26."

Available through Nov. 29, the Black Friday offer from Holland America Line is valid on more than 800 cruises to destinations worldwide, departing from December 2026 through spring 2029. The promotion includes up to 30% off cruise fares, free prepaid crew appreciation, 50% reduced deposits and free or reduced third and fourth guests in the same cabin. You can also combine the Black Friday offer with Holland America’s "Have it All" premium fare, which adds four high-value amenities: shore excursions, specialty dining, Wi-Fi and a beverage package.

Available through Dec. 2, Hurtigruten’s annual Black Friday sale offers savings of up to 50% on its 2027 Original Voyages, including the Coastal Express, which has cruised the Norwegian coast since 1893. Hurtigruten is also offering savings of up to 30% on its all-inclusive Signature Voyages in 2027, which include the North Cape Line and the Svalbard Line.

Through Dec. 2, HX Expeditions (formerly Hurtigruten Expeditions) is offering as much as 40% off select departures from late 2026 to 2028 with its Black Friday promotion. The sale offers savings on more than 50 all-inclusive expedition cruises to some of the world’s most remote destinations, including Antarctica, Greenland, Svalbard, the Galapagos Islands and the Northwest Passage.

Through Nov. 29, you can enjoy 60% off thanks to Black Friday savings on eligible itineraries through 2028 across the Jimmy Buffett-inspired Margaritaville at Sea fleet, plus third and fourth guests cruise for free on select sailings. These deals include sailings on the new Margaritaville at Sea Beachcomber, debuting in January 2027, as well as a buy-one-get-one deal on $499 Cruise Certificates that you can use on future voyages.

Through Nov. 30, receive a free veranda upgrade, plus a $250 onboard credit per cabin on eight Mitsui Ocean Cruises voyages sailing from February to April 2027. Mitsui operates two 458-guest, all-suite ships (formerly part of the Seabourn fleet) that are centered on authentic Japanese hospitality. It offers six- to 12-night itineraries in Japan that call on ports rarely visited by larger cruise lines. Both Japanese and English are spoken on board.

MSC Cruises' Black Friday sale is available through Nov. 27 and includes up to 40% off most 2027 itineraries around the world, plus up to $1,000 onboard credit, a free balcony upgrade and a "kids sail free" offer.

The Black Friday sale at Norwegian Cruise Line offers 50% off all cruises, plus a Free at Sea™ package. The offer is valid through Dec. 1 and applies to all itineraries, which visit nearly 350 destinations. The offer is good for all ships, including the cruise line’s two newest vessels: Norwegian Luna, which debuted in 2026, and Norwegian Aura, set to launch in spring 2027. Norwegian’s Free at Sea™ package on a standard seven-night sailing offers amenities that total more than $2,000 in savings. Such amenities include unlimited open bar access with premium spirits, unlimited Wi-Fi, three multicourse specialty dining meals for the first and second guest on the reservation, and $50 off each shore excursion for the first guest on the reservation.

Book by Dec. 1 to enjoy up to 50% savings on more than 200 Oceania Cruises voyages in 2027, thanks to the line’s Black Friday sale. The deal is available across the Oceania fleet, including its three newest ships: Oceania Vista (launched in 2023), Oceania Allura (launched in 2025) and Oceania Sonata (debuting in August 2027). Also included is Oceania Aurelia, the former Oceania Nautica, which is being refurbished and renamed ahead of its relaunch in late 2027.

Book during the Black Friday Savings event through Nov. 30 to save $1,500 to $10,000 per person on select 2027 Overseas Adventure Travel small ship ocean cruises. All 2027 departures are also eligible for savings of $500 per person plus an additional 10% when you pay in full. Discounted itineraries include small-ship adventures to Antarctica, the Baltic, the Adriatic, the Mediterranean, Egypt and the British Isles. Call 800-955-1925 and use code "BLACKFRIDAY26" to book.

The holiday sale from Tahiti-based Paul Gauguin Cruises offers savings of 10% on all 2027 departures to Polynesian destinations like the Society Islands, Tuamotus, Cook Islands and Marquesas. Cruises must be booked by Jan. 4, 2027.

Expedition cruise line Ponant Explorations has a holiday sale offering savings of up to 20% on most 2027 voyages in alliance with Smithsonian Journeys — the travel program of the Smithsonian Institution designed for immersive exploration and educational enrichment. Book through Jan. 4 using code "HOLIDAYSJ." The holiday sale also offers 10% savings on a wide selection of Ponant Explorations sailings to destinations such as the Panama Canal, Costa Rica and Madagascar. Use the code "HOLIDAY26" when booking.

Princess' “Blue Friday” sale runs through Dec. 7 and features up to 50% off cruise fares on select voyages to destinations such as the Caribbean, Alaska, Mexico, the Mediterranean and Asia. This includes itineraries on the cruise line’s two newest ships, Sun Princess and Star Princess. Additionally, third and fourth guests in a cabin sail free, and cruisers can enjoy up to $400 in instant savings.

From now until Dec. 3, save up to 40% on select Quark Expeditions voyages to the Arctic and Antarctica during its Black Friday sale. Limited cabins are available for Antarctic 2026-27 and Arctic 2027 expeditions, so check the deals if you’re looking to enjoy a polar expedition cruise to Patagonia and the Antarctic Peninsula or Greenland and Svalbard, Norway.

Luxury small-ship cruise line Regent Seven Seas Cruises is offering "The Black Friday Collection" — a limited-time offer of up to 40% savings on more than 60 voyages worldwide, including sailings in Europe, Alaska and Asia, if booked by Dec. 1. The promotion also includes $500 onboard credit per suite.

From Nov. 23 to Dec. 4, European river cruise line Riverside Luxury Cruises is offering 10% off full-board fares on select 2027 and 2028 sailings of five nights or longer during its Black Friday sale. You can combine this promotion with existing offers (Early Booking, Long Stay and Repeat Guest) for combined savings of up to 43%. All discounts will be applied at the time of booking; no code needed.

Through Dec. 7, U.K.-based Riviera Travel River Cruises is offering North American travelers a Black Friday sale with up to 50% off all 2027 and 2028 sailings and half-price deposits. For example, seven-night river cruises start at $1,999 per person (reduced from about $3,000 per person). Riviera will introduce two new ships in September 2027: MS Riviera Reflection on the Danube River and MS Riviera Alba on the Mekong River. It will also debut the world’s first solo-traveler-dedicated river ship, MS George Eliot, in June 2027. All Riviera ships qualify for Black Friday discounts.

Through Dec. 7, Royal Caribbean is offering Black Friday promotions and flash deals, including instant savings of up to $1,000 on select cruise fares, plus third and fourth guests in a cabin can sail free. These deals also include onboard credit starting at $150 and up to 50% savings on beverage packages, Wi-Fi and shore excursions. Savings, which vary by cabin and itinerary length, are available on more than 25 Royal Caribbean ships, including the line’s newest megaships — Legend of the Seas, Star of the Seas, Icon of the Seas and Utopia of the Seas. These ships sail to destinations in the Caribbean, Alaska and Europe.

Book by Nov. 29 to score Black Friday savings of up to 40% off cruise fares on select 2027 and 2028 river and ocean itineraries offered by Scenic Luxury Cruises and Tours. Scenic operates river ships and luxury expedition ocean vessels. Sale destinations include Europe’s top rivers, the Mediterranean and the Caribbean. To book, call Scenic’s reservations team at 844-323-1917.

Bookable through Dec. 8, the Black Friday deals from Seabourn Cruise Line are available for nearly all sailings through 2029 on Seabourn’s five luxury ships; offers include a free two-category Veranda Suite upgrade, plus up to a $2,000 shipboard credit per suite (for Penthouse Suites and above) and up to $500 shipboard credit per suite (for Oceanview and Veranda suites). The deal also includes a 15% reduced deposit on nearly all voyages.

Through Dec. 1, SeaDream Yacht Club, which operates two 112-guest yachts in the Caribbean, Mediterranean and Northern Europe, has a "Sail Away" promotion offering up to 25% off on select 2027 voyages. Use the code "SAILAWAY26" when booking.

With the Black Friday sale from luxury ocean and expedition line Silversea Cruises, you can save up to 45% on more than 850 sailings through May 2029 if you book by Dec. 7. By reserving now, you can also secure your suite with reduced deposits that start at 15%.

If you book a qualifying Star Clippers 2027 or 2028 Mediterranean voyage that visits Sicily by Dec. 31, the cruise line will offer a $500 (or $600 Canadian dollars) air credit and a complimentary 3GB Wi-Fi package per cabin. The offer is valid for North American residents booking a Category 2 to 6 cabin on one of Star Clippers' three sailing vessels: the 227-guest Royal Clipper, the 166-guest Star Clipper or the 166-guest Star Flyer. For qualifying sailings, reservations and questions, contact a travel adviser, call Star Clippers at 800-442-0551 or visit the Star Clippers website.

Through Dec. 4, expedition cruise line Swan Hellenic is offering up to $4,000 per person in Black Friday savings on 24 voyages worldwide, plus an additional $250 per person onboard credit. The eligible voyages sail to some of the world’s most remote places — including destinations in Antarctica, Africa, Asia Pacific and the Arctic — from March 9 to Oct. 27, 2027. Returning guests receive 10% loyalty savings, and back-to-back bookings earn a 5% discount.

Trafalgar has Black Friday deals, including BOGO 50%-off fares on featured European river sailings. The eligible 2027 itineraries, available through Dec. 3, change weekly (every Thursday), while other select departures are available at a 20% discount. Call 866-513-1995 to book, and make sure to mention Black Friday BOGO.

Luxury all-inclusive river cruise line Uniworld Boutique River Cruises — which offers sailings in Europe, Egypt, South America and Asia — has a Black Friday offer bookable through Dec. 18: The second guest pays 50% of the cruise fare when booking at double occupancy. This “Journey Together” offer is valid for select sailings throughout 2027 and is combinable with River Heritage Club member benefits for previous guests.

Family-owned, small-ship cruise line Variety Cruises has a Black Friday sale offering travelers up to 50% off on new reservations made through Dec. 7. Deals are available for seven-, 10- and 11-night cruises on Variety’s recently refurbished fleet of small ships (which hold no more than 49 guests). Available itineraries range from the Seychelles and Tahiti to signature Mediterranean voyages in Greece, Italy, Malta and destinations along the Adriatic coast.

Book any 2027 Victory Cruise Lines voyage by Nov. 30 to save $500 per person. Victory offers all-inclusive, small-ship cruises on the Great Lakes, coastal Canada, the U.S. East Coast and Florida.

While not technically a Black Friday promotion, Viking is offering its "lowest fares of the season" on select 2027 and 2028 river, ocean and expedition itineraries. River fares start at $1,999 per person, with reduced airfares and $25 deposits (just be sure to book by Nov. 27 with offer code "PLR27"). Ocean sailings are up to 35% off, with reduced airfare and $25 deposits (book by Nov. 30). Expedition voyages are up to 15% off, with reduced airfare and $25 deposits (book by Nov. 30).

Through Dec. 3, Virgin Voyages has a “buy one, get the second at 80% off” cruise fare promotion. Plus, you can score up to a $600 bar tab (depending on the length of the voyage) to cover onboard beverages. The deal is available for all cruises on Virgin’s four ships, including its first-ever Baltic sailings from Amsterdam on Valiant Lady in summer 2028. The promotion automatically applies when booking via the Virgin Voyages website.

Bookable through Dec. 2, the "Thankful for Travel Sales Event" offered by Windstar Cruises includes a complimentary all-inclusive package (which includes wine, beer, cocktails, Wi-Fi and gratuities, and is worth up to $1,386 per couple on a seven-night cruise). This applies to select sailings in the Mediterranean, Caribbean, Tahiti and Latin America through March 31, 2027. The promotion also lets you reserve with a $300 reduced deposit and gives you a $300 onboard credit.

In addition to booking directly with a cruise line, you can also reach out to a travel adviser to secure your reservation. Advisers have access to the same great deals that the lines are offering, but sometimes they can throw in extras, such as free bottles of wine or onboard credits. Before booking anything directly, it might be worth a phone call.

#6212. Aeromexico 787s Get Makeover With New Business Class, Premium Economy

Aeromexico is planning some major upgrades to its wide body fleet, which consists exclusively of Boeing 787s. This is interesting on many levels — we’ll see the larger Dreamliners get all-new business class cabins plus premium economy for the first time, we’ll see the smaller Dreamliners get the old business class cabins of the bigger Dreamliners, and we’ll see the airline adopt some Delta-style branding.

To start, let me provide the context that Aeromexico’s Boeing 787 fleet currently consists of 25 planes, including:

Aeromexico is planning on fully overhauling the premium cabins on these planes, as was announced by the company’s CEO at this week’s APEX FTE EXPO 2026.

The plan is for the 787-9s to get all-new cabins, and in the process, the 787-8s will get the old business class seats from the 787-9s. That means the 787-8s will get reverse herringbone seats, which are still competitive, but of course not cutting edge (though still a huge improvement over the pairs of seats currently on the planes).

The 787-9s will really become the next-generation flagship planes for the airline, though some patience will be required. The expectation is that the first of these Dreamliners will be retrofitted in the next 18 to 24 months (so hopefully by some point in 2028), and then it’ll likely take a couple of years for the fleet to be upgraded.

We’ll talk more about the new business class product as such in a bit, but the idea is that the 787-9s will get business class suites, including a front row “business class plus” product. On top of that, the 787-9s will be getting a premium economy cabin for the first time.

The plane will also have up to 70% more premium seats than before. Currently, Aeromexico’s 787-9s have 36 business class seats, while the retrofitted planes will have a total of 61 premium seats, between business class and premium economy. So I suspect the business class cabin won’t actually get that much bigger, but instead, most of that premium addition will come in the form of the new premium economy cabin.

It’s also worth mentioning that Aeromexico is adopting some Delta-style branding, as Delta owns a 20% stake in Aeromexico, and the two airlines have a close partnership.

Aeromexico’s new premium products will be known as Premier One Suites Plus (the “business class plus” product), Premier One Suites (business class), and Premier (premium economy). It seems the 787-8 business class will just be branded as Premier One, given the lack of suites with doors. That all sure seems to be inspired by the Delta One branding that’s used by the carrier’s partner.

Seth Miller from PaxEx.Aero flags how Aeromexico’s new Boeing 787-9 business class suite is from Recaro, as the airline is reportedly the launch customer for this new product. However, the exact product hasn’t actually been named.

Aeromexico CEO Dr. Andres Conesa unveiled the carrier's new premium economy cabin plus refreshed business class seat at #APEXFTEExpo in Singapore this week.Full teaser video in the story: paxex.aero/first-look-a….#PaxEx$RTX

I believe this might be an evolution of the Recaro R7 product (LATAM’s newest 787 business class), which in and of itself was already an evolution of the Recaro CL6720 product (Iberia’s newest A350 business class).

It seems that what was unveiled earlier this year was the new Recaro R7 Horizon concept, which is the same idea, but with upgraded technology and customization.

I imagine that we’ll learn more in the coming months, as this was an unusual way to unveil a new product. But this does seem to be officially happening, so it’s something to look forward to… down the road.

Aeromexico is planning some big upgrades to its Dreamliners. The Boeing 787-9s will be getting all-new cabins, including new business class suites, plus a premium economy cabin for the first time. There will even be a premium business product in the first row, with the products marketed as Premier One Suites Plus, Premier One Suites, and Premier.

As this happens, the 787-8s will be getting the old reverse herringbone seats from the 787-9s, so that will be a meaningful upgrade as well. You can expect these new cabins to roll out starting at some point in 2028, so some patience will be required. I can’t wait to learn more!

What do you make of Aeromexico’s Dreamliner plans?

Just flew the current 1-2-1 premier class on the 789 from LAX-MEX a few weeks ago (maybe Jessica Alba was a few rows behind me!). For what I was expecting, it was comfortable and did the trick. I love the idea of getting nicer seats for the longer flights and switching these out with the 2-2-2. I thought it was interesting that in the middle seats there was a gap where the partition could go up but nothing was there.

Can someone explain to me the benefit airlines get from announcing retrofits so far ahead of the actual completion date?

Any updates to their wifi? While I enjoyed having the life flat space from JFK-MEX, it was painful trying to get work done during the flight with the slow speeds.

Wait, do they mean that they will literally use the existing J seats from their 789 fleet and install them in the 788s instead of buying new seats of the same make and model ? I have never heard of that before !

Perfecto! 1-2-1 reverse herringbone (the 1’s facing the windows) will be a great improvement over the 2-2-2. LATAM has been doing similar cabin upgrades. More of this, everywhere, please! (LOT, TK, EK, etc., you fellas listening?)

#6211. UBI Breeds Dependence and Restricts Opportunity

The new Democratic Congress should walk away from the destructive path of this policy.

Democrats seized control of Congress, in part by focusing on affordability and the economy. An AP-NORC survey conducted just before the election found that both were ranked top issues for registered voters, outpacing the next most important issue, health care, by about 15 percentage points.

The new Democratic Congress will presumably pursue policies that are advertised as ways to reduce the cost of living. One idea they should reject is universal basic income (UBI). Leftists have long pushed for UBI, and the idea is gaining stream among tech leaders. It’s a policy that would backfire by reigniting inflation and ultimately harming those it attempts to help.

Joshua Bandoch is a research fellow with the Competitive Enterprise Institute, a free-market public-policy organization based in Washington, D.C.

Kevin Corinth is the Daniel C. Searle Chair and a senior fellow at the American Enterprise Institute.

#6210. Trump banks on personal relationships moving Putin, Xi toward U.S. interests

Russian President Vladimir Putin, Chinese President Xi Jinping and U.S. President Donald Trump arrive for a trilateral meeting in Shenzhen, China, on Thursday. (Win McNamee/AFP via Getty Images)

That was the greeting, complete with a lengthy handshake, President Donald Trump gave Vladimir Putin before two high-level meetings Thursday, including the first “trilateral” session with sitting U.S., Russian and Chinese heads of state.

“It’s nice to see you,” Trump told Putin before a private one-on-one meeting in China’s Shenzhen economic zone, before pulling the Russian strongman close and saying something into his ear too low for journalists’ microphones to pick up.

Trump and Putin then posed for the cameras with wide grins, again underscoring the U.S. president’s closeness with a world leader who has been partially shunned by the West since he launched a war with Ukraine in February 2022. Trump on Thursday also appeared several times alongside Chinese President Xi Jinping, who like Putin has been scorned by Republican and Democratic lawmakers for years.

“We’ve had a great relationship for many years. We've known each other for a long time. And I think a lot of wonderful things can come out of this — or, at least, start,” Trump told reporters as Putin beamed from a few feet away.

They later were joined by Xi for a group photo before sitting down at a round wooden table with a large arrangement of pink flowers in the center.

His interactions with and comments about Putin and Xi reflect Trump’s belief that his personal relationships can bend them toward U.S. interests. But that gambit clashed Thursday with his second term’s expiration date — the White House did not disclose any agreements reached during his various meetings with the two leaders, nor did Trump hold a press conference following the three-way session.

Both Putin and Xi are adept at playing the geopolitical long game. The 26 months left in Trump’s term is a relatively short amount of time compared to the duo that has been in power for a combined 56 years and will remain in place for the foreseeable future.

Indeed, even Trump acknowledged the first-ever meeting might not immediately yield much progress on its ostensible goal: paring each powers’ nuclear weapons arsenals.

“I must say, it's, quite frankly, a very hard thing to do, because once you have the nuclear weapons, it's very hard to not have them. It's very hard to give them up as the leader of a country,” Trump said as Putin and Xi looked on. “Something that's very difficult to say, because … it's the way life works.

“You know, you have thousands of weapons and you're supposed to give them up, and yet you have countries in addition to us, in much smaller numbers, but they have nuclear weapons, also,” he added. “So it's not an easy thing to do and give them up.”

Trump, who was convicted by a New York jury in a business records case and who saw a federal election interference case against him dismissed only because of his reelection, also appeared to join Putin’s resistance to international criminal justice entities that have alleged Putin has committed war crimes in Ukraine.

“In another area of potential cooperation between us, I'll be suggesting ways to protect our nations’ sovereignty from rogue globalist organizations such as the International Criminal Court, which has gotten out of control, which I believe we all agree has really strayed far from beyond its jurisdiction,” Trump said, a statement that would be almost unthinkable to hear from any other sitting U.S. president.

Other world leaders, including democratically elected ones, at two Pacific region economic summits in which Trump participated this week did not receive the kind of cordial and personal treatment from the U.S. side that Putin and Xi enjoyed.

And other world leaders and congressional Democrats this week expressed concern with Trump's closeness to the Russian and Chinese strongmen.

Senate Minority Leader Charles E. Schumer, D-N.Y., on Thursday called the unprecedented summit a “historic embarrassment.” He criticized Trump for leaving the meeting without any apparent concrete commitments from Moscow or Beijing on a number of issues, including curbing Chinese espionage inside U.S. companies and ending the Ukraine conflict.

“This summit was nothing but a glorified photo op and a gift to Putin and Xi,” Schumer said.

Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk wrote this Thursday on X, shortly after Trump’s warm greeting for the former KGB officer: “God, protect us from such friends.”

Nicolas Burns, a former senior U.S. diplomatic official under GOP and Democratic presidents, was critical of Trump’s meetings with Xi. He said it was “important” for U.S. and Chinese leaders to hold talks, but added: “We need stability in the relationship with China — but there’s a but.”

“The president seems to be following a detente policy with China, with very little substance. There’s a lot of pomp and circumstance, red carpets, a lot of nice words,” the former ambassador to China, NATO and Greece told “Morning Joe” on MS NOW. “Too friendly with Xi Jinping, who’s not going to be swayed by rosy words from President Trump.”

Even before Trump met with the Russian and Chinese leaders behind closed doors, Republican and Democratic lawmakers said they doubted very much would come from it.

“I want nuclear weapons to be reduced. As you know, China has been unwilling to even have a conversation with the United States about nuclear arms reduction until they reach a certain plateau in the number of weapons that they have,” House Armed Services Committee Vice Chair Rob Wittman, R-Va., told reporters Tuesday.

“I'm glad that they're willing to have the conversation. We do need a limit, as you know,” added Wittman, who lost his reelection bid earlier this month. “Right now, neither Russia nor China has a nuclear arms reduction treaty with the United States. It would be nice for us to actually have one.”

Sen. Richard Blumenthal, D-Conn., an Armed Services Committee member, wanted Trump to press Putin over Ukraine.

“Ukraine is defending itself from Putin's aggression, which this president should be opposing as well,” Blumenthal said Tuesday. “We are spending no money on Ukraine. Let's be very clear: Arms to Ukraine are purchased by Ukraine with financial support from Europe, not America. … Let's support Ukraine.”

On spending, Trump and administration officials have been pressing Senate Republicans to quickly pass another budget reconciliation measure with $350 billion more for the Defense Department. However, Senate Majority Leader John Thune, R-S.D., and other GOP senators have signaled in the last 24 hours that they had shelved the notion of another fast-track spending measure.

“You have to have a path forward. You've got to get on it, and you have to protect it, and that takes 50 in the Senate,” Thune told reporters Thursday. “And then you've got to get it through the House. As you probably saw yesterday, a lot of folks in the House were lobbing grenades at the Senate reconciliation bill and complaints about it not being offset, et cetera. So, you know, in my view at least, you want to have a path forward to success.”

John M. Donnelly and Jackie Wang contributed to this report.

#6209. Hah: Emirates Puts Auditors On Flights To “Provide Support & Guidance” To Crew

Emirates is known for its incredibly high service standards, and that’s largely thanks to the hierarchical system onboard. You have different ranks of flight attendants, then you have supervisors overseeing business class and economy, and then those supervisors report to the purser.

This system ensures that there’s accountability onboard, and I think that lack of hierarchy is one of the reasons we have service issues at airlines in the US, as no one is really in charge. Anyway, along those lines, Emirates has just introduced a new initiative, which will no doubt be controversial among flight attendants…

Emirates has a rank above pursers, which are the Standard Pursers (which is a weird name, but the idea is that they’re there to audit and enforce “standards”). These are specially trained former pursers who no longer work flights in a standard capacity (at least until now), but instead, they audit the crews onboard flights. They have completely different uniforms.

Emirates’ Chief Operations Officer, Adel Alredha, has just taken to Instagram to highlight a new initiative involving this small group of employees:

On 3 November, Emirates introduced a new initiative on select flights, which will have Standard Pursers work alongside cabin crew teams to provide support and guidance to ensure consistently high standards of service.

This step reflects the airline’s ongoing commitment to maintaining service quality and elevating the customer experience.

So rather than just auditing the cabins, these Emirates employees will actually be working in the cabin, and that’s sure to ruffle some feathers…

A post shared by Adel Alredha (@adelalredha)

Emirates is of course an incredibly global airline with staff from around the world, and I know a thing or two about the internal politics that crews deal with, the different working environments based on who is purser, etc.

For example, you have some pursers who are incredibly strict to the point that they make their colleagues feel uncomfortable and nervous, while you have other pursers who try to encourage good service by creating a fun environment, etc.

It goes without saying that historically when a flight had an auditor onboard, everyone would be on their absolute best behavior. In a way that’s no doubt a bit chaotic and stressful, since they’re worried about repercussions if something goes wrong.

When it comes to this initiative, on the one hand, it’s probably good for these auditors to get some renewed firsthand experience with service, guest expectations, etc. On the other hand, I have to imagine that from the perspective of other crew members, this won’t necessarily be perceived as an effort to “provide support and guidance.”

As one commenter on the Instagram post notes, “this is like sending a child to school along with mama with a stick to correct the kid every step.” Another commenter notes “as if there wasn’t already enough pressure on the crew.”

I am curious if these flights are still staffed with a regular purser in addition to this special rank of purser, because that could also cause a bit of a butting-of-heads. If an auditor is onboard in their official capacity, it’s clear what everyone’s role onboard is (everyone is there to make sure they perform well!). But if the auditor is there to simply “provide support,” that blurs the lines a little bit, no?

Anyway, there aren’t actually that many of these auditor pursers at the airline, so presumably only a small percentage of flights will have them. But if you do notice a crew member with a completely different uniform (more silver in color), now you know what’s going on. That would also be a great person to provide any feedback to, because they actually have the ability to get those details to the right person.

Emirates has Standard Pursers, who are essentially auditors who are assigned select flights, in order to evaluate service from the crew. As of this month, these auditors are also starting to work on flights alongside the crew, to “provide support and guidance.”

There’s no denying that this is an initiative that will make some crew members nervous, since this definitely blurs the line of auditing vs. having an extra set of helping hands. However, given the relatively small number of auditors, they shouldn’t be on too many flights. But if you do see someone in a completely different uniform (other than the standard female purser uniform), then now you know what’s going on.

What do you make of this Emirates initiative?

Why would an auditor on board create stress? If you are doing what you are supposed to be doing, then there would not be a problem. That auditor that write up how wonderfully well you performed your duties and are ready for promotion.

I am a predominantly ground based cabin crew manager for a large European airline but also work as supernumerary crew on 2-3 long haul flights per year. On those flights I wear a uniform and am additional to the crew complement and my role is to support and to a lesser degree assess member of my flying team. I find it really beneficial as airline crew are typically remote workers and rarely have access to their ground manager. It also gives me the ability to see first hand lots of the pain points my team complain to me about - service routines, galley layouts etc. I don't think these kind of roles are that unusual in the airline world. We just aren't called 'Standard Pursers' ouch.

If they're not "working" the flight, I could perceive this not going well with customers as well in a way: if you see people constantly passing by you and never checking on you, or if you ask that person for help and they direct it to another person, then it could come across the wrong way. Imagine you press the call attendant button and the Standard Purser just walks right by you. You'd probably think that you're being ignored by staff / they're slacking off.

If only all airlines had in-flight service auditors, the skies would be a better place.

Every company esp. a large service company can and should have employees that monitor the performance of frontline employees. This is both a reasonable and necessary job esp. for a company that has built its reputation on delivering high quality service. The reality is that the ME3 have had their businesses and their home local economies damaged enormously by the war w/ Iran which will be an endless thorn in their side; carriers such as Turkish as well as European carriers have benefitted greatly from being outside of the primary conflict zone. EK along w/ EY and QR have no choice but to do what it can to rebuild their businesses which have been set back decades; quality is the first thing that the ME3 can ensure is not eroded.

#6208. Bilt Rent Day Promotion December 2026: JetBlue Mosaic Status Challenge

Bilt is the platform known for providing rewards for housing payments. Earlier this year we saw massive changes at Bilt, including an overhaul of the credit card portfolio, plus new ways that housing rewards are offered.

There are many innovative things about Bilt, including that there’s a Bilt Rent Day promotion on the first day of each month. With a new month being right around the corner, I’d like to cover the details of the December 2026 Bilt Rent Day offer, as it includes both a JetBlue Mosaic elite status challenge, as well as an up to 100% bonus on statement credit redemptions (which isn’t a very good deal). It’s interesting to see a second month in a row with no transfer bonus…

There are a couple of aspects to the Bilt Rent Day promotion, including the ability to earn bonus points (which is the same every month), plus at least one additional promotion.

Note that Bilt Rent Day promotions are generally valid from 12:00AM ET until 11:59PM PT, so technically you have around 27 hours to take advantage of them.

Bilt has a portfolio of credit cards, including the no annual fee Bilt Blue Card (learn more), $95 annual fee Bilt Obsidian Card (learn more), and $495 annual fee Bilt Palladium Card (learn more) (Rates & Fees). Personally, I think the Bilt Palladium Card is by far the most lucrative.

On the first day of each month, you earn double those rewards on these cards, and earn up to 1,000 bonus points each month. It could be worth strategically making some purchases on the first day of each month to maximize this as much as possible.

For example, with double points, the Bilt Palladium Card offers 4x points on everyday spending on the first day of the month, so that’s pretty awesome (up to a cap of $500 worth of spending, since that would earn you 1,000 bonus points).

On December 1, 2026, Bilt is offering a bonus when members redeem points for statement credits. The bonus you’re eligible for depends on which Bilt credit card you have, as follows:

Let me cut to the chase — don’t redeem your points this way. It’s a bad value. Ordinarily you get 0.55 cents per Bilt point for statement credit redemptions, so even with a 100% bonus, you’re looking at getting 1.1 cents per point. Hard pass.

On December 1, 2026, Bilt is offering a JetBlue TrueBlue Mosaic status match challenge, and the status you’re eligible for depends on your Bilt elite status, as follows:

The status is matched for a period of three months, with no additional activity required to maintain it for that period. Then, during those three months, members can extend the status through January 31, 2028, by completing the following requirements:

Regardless of which tier you initially match to, the status you get to keep is based on the activity over the course of those three months. As a reminder, you earn one tile for every $100 spent on JetBlue, or every $1,000 spent on a co-branded JetBlue credit card. So renewing status requires anywhere from $1,000 to $4,000 of airfare spending, or $10,000 to $40,000 of credit card spending.

This of course comes at a generally useful time for JetBlue elite status, given that the airline is introducing first class, with space available upgrades being an elite perk. However, it’s worth emphasizing that this really isn’t such a special offer, as it’s basically just JetBlue’s standard status match challenge offer. Except in this case, you can unlock it with Bilt elite status rather than airline elite status.

On the first day of each month, Bilt offers a Rent Day promotion. In addition to earning up to double points for purchases, for December 2026, there are two offers members can take advantage of.

One offer is for up to a 100% bonus on statement credit redemptions, which can get you at most 1.1 cents per point of value. Please don’t redeem your points that way. JetBlue is also offering a status match challenge, whereby Bilt members can receive Mosaic 1 or Mosaic 2 status for a period of 90 days, and can then extend status through early 2028, with the opportunity to earn up to Mosaic 3 status, based on how many tiles are earned.

Are you taking advantage of the Bilt Rent Day promotion for December 2026?

#6207. Why Aerolíneas Argentinas Is Basically An Ultra Low Cost Carrier In Disguise

This might seem like a rather niche topic to cover in my first week at OMAAT, but after Ben mentioned this story in his intro article, I thought it made sense to follow up fast with an explainer.

As a flag carrier of the 3rd most populous nation in South America, I went into my Aerolíneas Argentinas flight with them at the start of the year expecting some pretty standard things: enjoying my SkyTeam benefits, lounge access, and, most importantly of all for someone living out of a suitcase, checked bag allowance.

However, I quickly discovered that the airline is basically an ultra-low-cost airline masquerading as a full-service carrier.

I needed to get from Buenos Aires to Mendoza for a friend’s 40th birthday celebrations. Options were pretty limited, with nonstop flights available with either JetSmart or, indeed, Aerolíneas Argentinas. I try to avoid low-cost airlines when possible, because, quite simply, I enjoy the flying experience, and low-cost airlines tend to suck every enjoyable element out of it.

Other pros to booking Aerolíneas Argentinas, personally:

After researching my options, I used Flying Blue miles to book two single tickets from Buenos Aires Jorge Newbery Aeroparque Airport (AEP) to Mendoza’s El Plumerillo Airport (MDZ).

I can’t remember how much the fares were when I was planning the trip, but each one-way flight cost a total of 7,500 miles and less than $10 in taxes and fees.

Looking now at example fares for January next year, round-trips for Aerolíneas’ lowest and most restrictive fare category (more on that to come) start at around $120.

I know it’s not a hard-and-fast rule, but I’ve come to expect that, most of the time, the baggage allowance listed on the booking confirmation is correct. This is often true with redemptions, such as British Airways, which notably offers and acknowledges a 23 kg baggage allowance when redeeming Avios, even for a short-haul flight in economy.

The confirmation email I received clearly noted 1x checked bag with a 23 kg limit.

Again, the attached PDF stated that I’d have 1x checked bag included.

As the Argentinian scamsters would have it, I learned at check-in that the airline has a 15 kg weight limit for checked bags on domestic flights. I tried to plead my case and showed the rather unhelpful check-in agent my booking confirmation, but he basically said, “that means nothing.”

So they weigh your bag, give you a ticket, and then you have to exit the terminal building and find this little cashier where they collect their scammy little earnings. And what better place to proudly display a “SkyTeam Alliance Member” sign at the very desk where the airline also proudly collects baggage fees from SkyTeam elite status holders, even when traveling on award tickets?

Once I’d been charged the fee of around $17, I had to join another queue back inside and show them I’d paid for the extra weight before they’d dispatch my bag. You might look at the $32 in fees I paid and think, “What is he complaining about?” But this isn’t about the actual amount of money; it’s the principle.

Only after the debacle did I learn the extent of Aerolíneas Argentinas’ domestic fare restrictions. Imagine paying $510 (more than four times the cheapest fare) for a “premium economy” ticket and still only getting 15 kg checked baggage allowance, no Fast Pass, no priority boarding (what?), and no lounge access. The latter isn’t such a big deal as Aerolíneas Argentinas doesn’t even have its own lounge at AEP.

Airline loyalty is really important to me, and I generally value it more than the ability to redeem miles. Maybe I’ll get into that another day…

Things got off to a fairly normal start when I saw the Sky Priority check-in kiosks at Aeroparque.

That feeling of normalcy lasted as long as it took me to get from the sign to the aforementioned conversation about the checked bag situation at the desk. Despite my very best efforts combining my Castilian Spanish and Geordie charm (we’re called Geordies where I’m from in the North East of England), the man at the check-in desk seemed to take real pleasure in explaining that the checked bag rules on my booking confirmation were irrelevant and I’d have to pay the fee.

For what it’s worth, Sky Priority check-in was also available at Mendoza.

Being nickel-and-dimed for a checked bag by a flag carrier airline is shameful.

Back at Aeroparque, there was no fast track, and the security line was ridiculously long. That said, it’s rare in South America to have fast track lanes. For example, no matter whether you’re flying economy or first class (even Air France La Première), everyone waits in the same line to clear pre-departure passport control at São Paulo’s Guarulhos.

Thanks to my Priority Pass, I did have access to the surprisingly nice AMAE lounge in the national departures part of the airport.

Even from the outside, my 15-year-old Embraer 190 looked like it had seen better days. The zebra-striped dirt streaks running from each window suggested this place hadn’t been washed or hit the maintenance hangar for a while.

Inside the Embraer, however, could have been a lot worse. The older seats had thick padding, and despite being a small 2-2-configured cabin, it felt bright and spacious.

It was the Uber advertising on every single headrest that I found most jarring.

The legroom was decent, too. The retro seatback screens, on the other hand, were pretty much redundant.

It was stepping on board the 16-year-old Boeing 737-700 back to Buenos Aires that Aerolíneas Argentinas’ low-costness was most glaring. Looking at this, I would never guess this plane belonged to a flag carrier. The seats were very uncomfortable, and I think I remember they didn’t recline either.

As for service, I don’t recall it being particularly good or particularly bad. Forgettable is probably the most accurate word.

Imagine the likes of Spirit (RIP) or Ryanair calling itself a national flag carrier; that’s basically what Aerolíneas Argentinas is. I’m planning a trip with my dad and brother for February next year that includes Argentina, and I will actively avoid flying Aerolíneas, even if it means forgoing the chance to earn any Flying Blue miles and XPs.

It’s almost as if the airline has been abandoned. After all, the only real competition is low-cost airlines at LATAM — the full-service carrier which dominates South America. Who knows, maybe things will change come 2028 when it takes delivery of new Airbus A330-900s and Boeing 737 MAXs.

If I were a power that be at SkyTeam, I’d definitely remove the airline from the alliance. And if I had my way, Aerolíneas Argentinas would be bought by LATAM, and the cherry on top would be LATAM joining SkyTeam. I should probably put a business case together for that…

Hi Daniel! Great review but I’m afraid I might have to disagree a little with you here based on my personal experiences with AR this April and November. The hand luggage allotment seems designed specifically to rope passengers into this fee, given the sizing relative to what appeared to me to be very generously-sized overhead bins on board compared with what is standard in America. I actually wasn't that surprised by the flight. It was clean, reasonably comfortable, and it's a v short flight. #6206. End Of An Era: American Retires Boeing 777 Flagship First Class

American Airlines has just officially “retired” its Flagship First product on the Boeing 777-300ER, meaning that no US carrier offers an international first class product anymore. The good news is that an updated business class product is in the process of being rolled out, and that’s something that should benefit a lot of travelers.

As I’ve covered in the past, American is in the process of eliminating its “premium” first class product, and that change was just implemented for flights as of this week on the carrier’s biggest planes.

Specifically, the Boeing 777-300ER is American’s “flagship” aircraft, with 20 of the planes in the fleet. As of this week, the airline is no longer selling first class on these planes. Now, plenty of 777-300ERs with these cabins are still flying around, as American has just started reconfiguring its 777-300ERs with new cabins, including the new business class.

Still, for flights effective immediately, first class seats are just being sold as standard business class seats, and any business class passenger can select seats in the first two rows (you’d think they’d try to charge extra or at least reserve them for select elite members, but nope). So there will no longer be a differentiated soft product… not that there was much of a difference as of late anyway!

I expect we’ll continue to see these planes flying around well into late 2027, or possibly even into 2028, depending on how fast the retrofit project happens. American’s dedicated first class ground product has also largely been discontinued, as Flagship First Dining has turned into Flagship Dining, so a la carte lounge dining is now available to eligible business class passengers as well.

It’s great that these planes will be getting new business class suites, as they’ll also be the aircraft belonging to a US carrier with the most business class seats, as they’ll have 70 of them… that’s lot!

While American has now eliminated its international first class product, it’s worth emphasizing that the airline still technically has a “premium” first class, in the sense of a cabin above business class.

Specifically, American still has its specially configured Airbus A321T aircraft, which are used primarily for flights between New York (JFK) and Los Angeles (LAX) and San Francisco (SFO). The planes have 10 reverse herringbone seats spread across five rows, in a 1-1 configuration.

American also plans to eliminate this product, as the A321Ts will be reconfigured into standard A321 domestic configuration aircraft, and A321XLRs will be taking over the transcon routes.

American has stopped selling first class on these planes for flights as of March 28, 2027. After that date we’ll still see some of the planes flying with the cabins, but the first class seats will simply be sold as business class.

American Airlines has officially eliminated its international first class product, as Boeing 777-300ERs no longer have Flagship First for sale. These planes are being retrofitted, as first class seats are being eliminated, and new business class suites are being introduced. However, the planes will keep flying around with the current cabins for quite some time, and business class passengers can freely assign the first class seats.

In the spring, we’ll see American eliminate its last “premium” first class product, which is the A321T first class cabin, as those planes are replaced by A321XLRs.

What do you make of the end of American’s Flagship First on the 777?

Citi Shop takes some of the work out of saving money online. Once you've installed its browser extension, it acts as a shopping portal and coupon hunter all-in-one, rewarding you with statement credits.

It has broad reach, too, with more than 5,000 participating online merchants. That's easier than a traditional online shopping portal, which requires you to remember to start at the portal and click through before filling your cart.

Its ease of use makes it a great resource, but other portals or special discounts may save you more.

Here's how Citi Shop works and what to consider to determine if it's the best savings path for you.

Citi Shop is a free browser extension for primary cardholders with an eligible Citi credit card, including ThankYou points cards and cobranded cards. Citi retail and commercial cards are usually ineligible.

Offers come as either a percentage back or a fixed amount back, and your earnings are applied as a statement credit on the Citi card you selected during enrollment.

Citi Shop is separate from Citi Merchant Offers, which requires you to enroll in targeted offers with a specific Citi card and then use that card for the qualifying purchase.

Both Citi Shop and traditional portals give you an extra reward for making purchases they track.

But Citi Shop brings potential rebates to you, rather than requiring you to initiate your savings search. The extension automatically displays a pop-up with an available offer when you visit a participating website. You'll have the option to activate the offer before checkout.

All of Citi Shop's rebates are provided as statement credits, unlike the potential airline miles, hotel points or credit card rewards of traditional portals.

What I like about Citi Shop is that it also acts like a shopping assistant. Instead of opening six coupon sites only to discover that every code expired last Tuesday, it handles the scavenger hunt for you and tests available promo codes on your behalf.

Like Capital One Shopping, Citi Shop uses a browser extension. However, Capital One Shopping doesn't require a Capital One card to enroll and its rewards can be redeemed for eligible gift cards instead of a statement credit.

Generally speaking, Citi Shop clashes with other shopping portals. Both work by referring and tracking your purchase, so they can be mutually exclusive. You'll need to make your purchase through whichever offer is better.

Related: Chase shopping portal guide: How to earn bonus Ultimate Rewards points

Unless Citi Shop finds a promo code, it won't lower your total at checkout. Its returns arrive later as statement credits and may require patiently waiting two to six months, sometimes longer.

Even though you need an eligible Citi card to enroll, you don’t have to pay with it. Citi allows any payment method accepted by the merchant.

I really appreciate the flexibility to choose the best card for each purchase. For electronics, I might pick a card with an extended warranty while I might stick to a travel rewards credit card for hotel bookings. You can even pay with a gift card if you wish.

Regardless of how you pay, the statement credit will post to the Citi card you enrolled.

If you have an eligible Citi card but rarely remember to click through a shopping portal, Citi Shop is an easy win. Install it, activate offers when the pop-up appears and let the credits come to you. That convenience can also be a big benefit if you have partners or other family members who aren't as motivated to strategize on rewards as you are.

But with a little extra effort, you might be able to earn even more. When the Citi Shop pop-up appears with an offer, take a minute to compare before you click Activate.

Checking a shopping portal aggregator such as Cashback Monitor shows payouts from multiple cash-back, airline and credit card portals, making it easier to compare a Citi Shop statement credit with points or miles elsewhere.

Suppose a $200 jacket is marked down to $160. Citi Shop finds a $10 coupon, bringing the checkout price to $150, and offers 8% back. Assuming the full amount qualifies, you'd receive a $12 Citi Shop credit. If you pay with a card that earns 2% back and has an activated merchant offer for $5 off a $100 purchase, you'd collect another $8. After all the credits and rewards post, your net cost would be $130.

Read the terms before getting too excited. Some brands, products, gift cards or coupon codes may be excluded and you might not be able to stack every layer every time. Still, you can often use multiple discounts simultaneously for a better deal.

Citi Shop is not a program for instant gratification. Citi says statement credits post 61 to 180 days after a completed purchase, though some can take longer.

In many cases, offers may show as pending long before they officially pay out, to account for potential returns. Hotel rewards may remain pending until after the stay. Eventually, you'll see it on your statement as "CITI SHOP STATEMENT CREDIT."

If a credit hasn't posted after the expected window, contact Citi using the number on the back of your enrolled card. You may want to keep good records along the way, like a screenshot of the offer and an e-receipt from the purchase.

Citi Shop's biggest advantage is convenience. It does the heavy lifting by reminding you to activate offers so you don't miss out on earnings from your online orders, while testing coupon codes along the way. The offers themselves may or may not be the highest available, but they are certainly the easiest.

To truly optimize your returns, you'll want to compare Citi Shop earnings with those from other shopping portals — and stack other forms of saving along the way. But when that sounds like too much, the ease of this extension can still be a great way to tack on some extra returns.
